speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Some countries will respond by home-shoring certain production, while others will strengthen their inter-dependence with other economies and diversify their supply chains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: How people travel will also change in ways more significant than after 9/11.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Companies will need to transform their business models and operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Manufacturers will have to redesign their "just-in-time" production to balance between achieving efficiency and resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The pace of digitalisation will accelerate and play a more fundamental role in the way we work, live and play.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We need to find our new relevance to the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Even as we cope with the immediate challenges, there will be new opportunities where we can seize, we can leverage on our strengths and we can ride on the key shifts brought about by the pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: While some of these developments are still playing out, and there is still some uncertainty in terms of how the new landscape will look like, there are a few areas our businesses and workers should start to re-position ourselves for.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: While the pandemic is still evolving, some changes, including those that started even before COVID-19, have become evident, such as a renewed emphasis on health and an increased focus on sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: If this continues, it will benefit industries such as healthcare, online retail and financial services – just to name a few.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We will have the opportunity to enhance our value proposition in these areas to capture the growth in demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: As Asia continues to grow, we must also work together with our neighbours to capture new opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: For example, in the agri-food industry, we are building up our local food production capabilities and also working with neighbouring countries such as Brunei, to grow this as an exportable sector that can strengthen food security and create good jobs for our peoples.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This started before COVID-19, and we can expect the pace to accelerate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: As companies shift their production lines, our manufacturing and logistics industries should position themselves to serve new demand and participate in new supply chains that are formed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We must continue to compete on our strengths such as trust, quality and connectivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: These have become even more important to investors and customers in the new environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This is where our biomedical and precision engineering industries can play to our advantage by leveraging sophisticated technologies and the trust and quality that have been associated with Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Our trusted brand name is an asset in this environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: If we can move fast to capture the opportunities created by these shifts, Singapore will be in a stronger position when recovery comes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The pandemic has compelled businesses in all industries to turn to technology-enabled platforms for safe operations and business continuity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Besides shoring up a strong demand for digital solutions in the ICT sector, the quickened pace of technology adoption across industries has also transformed business models – especially for traditionally brick-and-mortar industries such as retail and food services – and it has enabled these businesses to access wider markets and consumer segments than before.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: For essential services such as healthcare, the rise of tele-medicine also provides an opportunity for the industry to redefine service quality and access markets beyond Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We can recover from this crisis and we will grow again.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The road ahead will not be easy, but we will walk this journey together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The key is to remain united and support one another to transform ourselves to seize new opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We need to strengthen Singapore’s attractiveness as a hub for business and investments and remain open to global trade and talent to benefit from Asia’s growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: How well we recover will depend on our adaptability as a country, as businesses and also as individuals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We start from solid foundations – a trusted brand name and rule of law, a cohesive and hardworking people, a strong tripartite partnership and excellent connectivity with the rest of the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: With these strong fundamentals, I am confident that Singapore will survive the crisis and we can emerge stronger.
